evals.prompt: We publish AirCare Journal (aircare-journal.example), an independent indoor-air-quality publication, and want a full domain-authority baseline before our autumn GEO push. Run the complete 40-item CITE audit as a Content Publisher. Everything our team could pull is in evals/files/pack-aircare-journal-content-publisher-en.md plus the top-25 backlink export in evals/files/backlinks-aircare-journal-top25-export.csv — no tools are connected in this session, so those two files are the entire data set. We want the veto check, all four dimension tables, the weighted CITE Score with the calculation shown, and the Top 5 priority improvements.
evals.expected_output: A full 40-item CITE report built solely from the pack and CSV: veto check clean (T03 pass — 1,240 referring domains proportional to 46,200 monthly organic visits; T05 pass — max profile overlap 18%; T09 pass — Search Console shows no manual actions), so the CITE Score is uncapped and its rating label matches the scale. Content Publisher weights (C 40% / I 15% / T 20% / E 25%) are stated and used. Per-item grades follow the benchmark bands on the pack's labeled populations — C01 Pass on the 1,240 unique referring domains (not the 18,644 total backlinks), C05/C07 Partial on the 4-query/2-engine AI test, T06 Partial on the privacy-protected-but-stable WHOIS, I09/I10 Fail on 6 unlinked mentions and zero autocomplete association. Every dimension score equals the sum of its ten item points and the CITE Score recomputes from them under the stated weights. Top 5 improvements are impact-sorted with Finding/Evidence/Impact/Fix and confidence labels. Every number in the report traces to the pack or the CSV.
expectations: C01 is graded Pass on the correct population: the evidence cites the pack's 1,240 unique referring domains against the benchmark's C01 Pass standard (>=500 unique referring domains) — not the 18,644 total backlinks, which the pack explicitly labels as the link count, not the domain count — matching the benchmark's common-mistake rule 'Count unique referring domains, not total link count'.

Mid-band and weak-signal items are graded to the benchmark bands the fixture data lands in, with the fixture numbers cited: C05 Partial (cited on 4 distinct queries — inside the 3-9 Partial band), C07 Partial (cited by exactly 2 AI engines), T06 Partial (WHOIS privacy-protected but reputable registrar and ownership stable since 2017 — the benchmark's 'Privacy-protected but reputable and stable' Partial band, not Pass, which requires public WHOIS), I09 Fail (6 unlinked mentions — below the <10 Fail threshold), and I10 Fail (the brand appeared in 0 of 8 autocomplete checks — no measurable association).

The veto check covers all three veto items and is clean, with fixture evidence: T03 Pass (1,240 referring domains proportional to 46,200 monthly organic visits — the export's coherence flag reads normal), T05 Pass (maximum shared-referring-domain overlap 18%, far under the >60% Fail threshold), T09 Pass (Search Console 'No issues detected' for manual actions, no deindexing history); no cap is applied, the final CITE Score is reported uncapped, and its rating label matches the reported number on the benchmark scale (90-100 Excellent | 75-89 Good | 60-74 Medium | 40-59 Low | 0-39 Poor).

The Content Publisher weight profile is applied and stated: C 40% / I 15% / T 20% / E 25% per the domain-type weight table — not the default 35/20/25/20 — and the score-calculation line shows the weighted formula (CITE Score = C x w_C + I x w_I + T x w_T + E x w_E) with those weights.

Score arithmetic is recomputable from the report's own grades, rounding defined: all 40 items are scored (this pack leaves nothing unmeasurable, so no N/A is needed), each dimension score equals the sum of its ten reported item points (Pass=10, Partial=5, Fail=0), and the reported CITE Score equals the weighted sum of the report's own four dimension scores under the stated weights — exact at one decimal, or within 0.5 if the report rounds to an integer; a CITE Score that cannot be reproduced from the report's own tables fails.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every metric in the report — referring-domain counts, DR values, traffic, citation counts, review scores, percentages — appears in the pack or the CSV; no DA/DR, backlink, search-volume, or AI-citation figure is invented (no tools are connected — absent tools mean absent numbers); no item outside the 40 CITE IDs is introduced and no CORE-EEAT content items are mixed in; the Top 5 improvements each carry Finding/Evidence/Impact/Fix with a Confirmed/Likely/Hypothesis confidence label, every Hypothesis names what would confirm it, and every Evidence field cites fixture data.

Derived-figure arithmetic is self-consistent: every figure the report computes rather than copies from the pack — item tallies and counts, points-scored/points-lost sums, 'total achievable' or 'points on the table' claims, Top 5 potential-gain figures, and any aggregate or projection built on them — recomputes from the report's own per-item grades (Pass=10 / Partial=5 / Fail=0) and its own stated weights. Concretely: a stated count equals the number of items it enumerates in the same sentence or table; a points total equals the sum of the grades it totals; each potential gain equals that item's recoverable points (10 from a Fail, 5 from a Partial) times its dimension's stated weight; and a combined-gain claim equals the sum of the individual gains it aggregates. This eval's pack supports all 40 items, so any 'X of 400 raw points' or 'N Pass / N Partial / N Fail' summary must reconcile with the report's own 40 rows and with itself (points lost = Partials x 5 + Fails x 10). A derived figure that contradicts the report's own tables fails, even where every source metric is correctly traced to the pack. Out of scope here because they are graded above: the four dimension scores and the weighted CITE Score. Not derived figures: framework constants (the 39 veto cap, rating-band boundaries, benchmark item thresholds). If the report states no derived figure beyond the dimension scores and the CITE Score, this expectation passes.
